title: Whole-Roos normalization of point-system transport and sections
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and on the small pro-etale site set $B_n=(A_n)_s$ and $\widehat R_s=\lim_nB_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_s$ be the abelian category of strict $B_n$-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, with its ordinary unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $U_s$ for levelwise restriction to $\widehat R_s$-module towers and $\mathcal L_s=R\lim U_s$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Put $F_r=(h^r)^{-1}$ on module complexes with scalars transported through the canonical coefficient isomorphisms, and $G_r$ for its levelwise functor on systems [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Read the finite levels through $j_{r,M}:F_rM\to(h^r)^*M$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, of part (a) of the latter definition. Let $\Gamma_\bullet$ be restriction of scalars followed by exact sections levelwise, retaining all transitions [def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

Use the natural maps $u_{r,M}$ and their localizations $I_{r,C}$ specified by [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent]. For a strict tower complex $X$ of $\widehat R_s$-modules, or of $R$-modules, write
$$H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1],\quad H(X)^i=(\prod_nX_n^{i-1})\oplus(\prod_nX_n^i),\quad d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da),$$
where $s_X((x_n)_n)=(t_nx_{n+1})_n$ for the actual transitions $t_n$. Use the natural normalized identification of this functor with TOTAL derived limit [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; its strict augmentation has zero shifted coordinate. Countable products of sheaf modules are sectionwise and exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], as are products of $R$-modules.

For every $C\in D(\mathscr S_s)$, with no completeness or constructibility restriction on $N=\mathcal L_sC$, the canonical product comparisons for $F_r$ and $\Gamma(s,-)$ give natural isomorphisms
$$a_{r,C}:F_r\mathcal L_sC\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_sG_rC,\qquad \zeta_C:R\lim\Gamma_\bullet C\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,\mathcal L_sC).$$
Their normalization is that of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]: on a strict representative $M$, $a$ is the canonical $F_r(\prod X_n)\cong\prod F_rX_n$ comparison on BOTH coordinates of $H(U_sM)$ (including the level identifications $j_r$), and $\zeta$ is the inverse of the analogous exact-sections comparison. There is no off-diagonal component. Equivalently these are the comparisons obtained by applying inverse image or sections to the entire limit cone on tower resolutions.

Let $\sigma_{r,K}:\Gamma(s,K)\to\Gamma(s,F_rK)$ denote the restriction/colimit-insertion/sheafification recipe of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] on any completed-module complex $K$, localized by exactness. Then, as an equality of derived maps on WHOLE towers,
$$\zeta_{G_rC}\circ R\lim(I_{r,C})=\Gamma(s,a_{r,C})\circ\sigma_{r,\mathcal L_sC}\circ\zeta_C.$$
More explicitly, on a strict representative, $R\lim(I_{r,C})$ in these normalized coordinates is the actual diagonal chain map
$$H(u_r)(b,a)=((\prod_nu_{r,n})b,(\prod_nu_{r,n})a),\qquad (1-s_{\Gamma_\bullet G_rM})\prod_nu_{r,n}=(\prod_nu_{r,n})(1-s_{\Gamma_\bullet M}).$$
Here $u_{r,n}$ is the $n$th map after sections, so $H(u_r)$ is between the $R$-module tower cones. After the canonical product comparisons, restriction on each product is $(x_n)_n\mapsto(x_n|_{h^r})_n$ on both coordinates. All the comparisons and the displayed equality are natural for morphisms in $D(\mathscr S_s)$.

proof.text: Fix $r\geq1$ and a complex $M$ of strict systems representing $C$. Put $X=U_sM$ and $Y=U_sG_rM$. The scalar identity $\pi_nc_{\widehat R}=c_nF_r(\pi_n)$ identifies $Y$ with the levelwise image $F_rX$, through the specified $j_{r,M_n}$, including its actual transitions. Indeed restriction of the $B_n$-action along $\pi_n$ before or after transport gives the same $\widehat R_s$-action by this identity. The site equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] computes inverse image by $(F_rQ)(V,v)=Q(V,h^rv)$. Thus its canonical product comparison is an isomorphism, obtained by evaluating products at $(V,h^rv)$. Transport through the ring isomorphism of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] preserves this formula and exactness, also for completed modules. We therefore have an additive exact product-preserving functor $F_r$ on the ambient completed-module category, without any normalization hypothesis on $M$.

proof.text: Let $T=\Gamma(s,-)$ with the $R$-action induced by constant sections. This is additive and exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Sectionwise products from [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] give the canonical isomorphism $T(\prod Q_n)=\prod T(Q_n)$, with its ordinary projection maps. Restricting the resulting section modules to $R$ leaves their underlying groups, products and exactness unchanged. The levelwise functor $T^{\operatorname{Tow}}X$ is exactly $\Gamma_\bullet M$, with the same transitions, by [def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations]. Countable products are exact in the sheaf-module category by the cited product lemma. They are exact in $R$-modules as well: kernels and images of product maps are coordinatewise, and a tuple in a product of surjection targets lifts by choosing a preimage in each coordinate. In applying the general ringed-site comparison to $T$, ordinary $R$-modules are sheaf modules on the one-object site with the trivial topology.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] for these strict towers, in the total-derived-limit sense of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], to write $\theta_X:\mathcal L_sC\xrightarrow{\sim}H(X)$ and $\eta_X:R\lim(T^{\operatorname{Tow}}X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(T^{\operatorname{Tow}}X)$. The comparisons are natural for strict maps and descend to the derived tower category; their strict augmentation is $z\mapsto(0,(\gamma_nz)_n)$. To match the signed coordinates in [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit], use $J_X(b,a)=(a,-b)$. Direct computation gives $J_Xd(b,a)=(da,db+(1-s_X)a)=dJ_X(b,a)$ for its differential $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s_X)x-dy)$. The augmentation becomes $((\gamma_nz)_n,0)$, exactly its normalization. Conjugating a diagonal product comparison by $J$ leaves it diagonal with the same comparison on both coordinates.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] to $F_r$ and to $T$, whose hypotheses were checked in Steps 1 and 2. Write $\kappa^F_X:F_rH(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(Y)$ and $\kappa^T_X:T H(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(T^{\operatorname{Tow}}X)$ for their diagonal product comparisons. The specified maps are
$$a_{r,C}=\theta_Y^{-1}\kappa^F_XF_r(\theta_X),\qquad \zeta_C=T(\theta_X^{-1})(\kappa^T_X)^{-1}\eta_X.$$
These have the asserted sources and targets because $Y=U_sG_rM$. The lemma identifies these particular maps with comparison of the entire ordinary limit cone on tower resolutions, independently of the resolutions. It supplies naturality, invertibility and the zero-shifted-coordinate augmentation normalization, rather than just the existence of an unspecified isomorphism. Step 3 puts its formula in precisely the coordinates required here.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: base-change isomorphisms at stage E are rationalizations of the integral ones; prerequisite prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model proof (3), integral maps are derived limits of levelwise composites; extracted old item steps 5-6. Agent-formulated refinement of the explicit inverse-image and point-transport recipes; not a verbatim theorem of the blueprint. Whole-cone comparison argument below, written by Q127; supporting total-limit model: Stacks Tag 0941, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok.

proof.text:
By [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent], $u=u_{r,M}$ is a strict chain map $T^{\operatorname{Tow}}X\to T^{\operatorname{Tow}}Y$ representing $I_{r,C}$. Set $P=\prod_nu_{r,n}$ and write $t_n,t'_n$ for the source and target transitions after sections. The $n$th coordinate of $(1-s')P(x)$ is $u_{r,n}x_n-t'_nu_{r,n+1}x_{n+1}=u_{r,n}(x_n-t_nx_{n+1})$, since $t'_nu_{r,n+1}=u_{r,n}t_n$. Thus $(1-s')P=P(1-s)$. Together with $dP=Pd$ this gives
$$d(Pb,Pa)=(-Pdb-P(1-s)a,Pda)=H(u)d(b,a).$$
Consequently $H(u)(b,a)=(Pb,Pa)$ is the actual cone map, with no off-diagonal term. Naturality of the normalized comparison in [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies it with $R\lim(I_{r,C})$, namely $\eta_YR\lim(I_{r,C})=H(u)\eta_X$.

proof.text: The recipe of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] makes sense termwise for every completed-module complex $K$. In the reindexing description of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], its colimit insertion and sheafification identify $\sigma_{r,K}$ with restriction $K(s,\mathrm{id})\to K(s,h^r)$. This is the same identification of the inverse-image recipe used in [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent]; it applies to any sheaf, independently of boundedness. It is $R$-linear: restriction of a constant $a\in R$ is the same constant after the coefficient identification, as can be checked after every $\pi_n$ using $\pi_nc_{\widehat R}=c_nF_r(\pi_n)$. For any sheaf-module map $f:K\to K'$, the presheaf identity $f_{(s,h^r)}\operatorname{res}_{h^r}=\operatorname{res}_{h^r}f_{(s,\mathrm{id})}$ proves naturality, and for $f=d^i$ proves the chain-map identity. Exactness of $T$ and $F_r$ therefore localizes this natural transformation to all ambient derived complexes, including $\mathcal L_sC$.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: base-change isomorphisms at stage E are rationalizations of the integral ones; prerequisite prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model proof (3), integral maps are derived limits of levelwise composites; extracted old item steps 5-6. Whole-cone comparison argument below, written by Q127; supporting total-limit model: Stacks Tag 0941, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok.

proof.text:
Put $Z=H(X)$. The preceding restriction formula and the defining projection equations for the product comparisons give the chain-map equality
$$(\kappa^T_Y)^{-1}H(u)=T(\kappa^F_X)\sigma_{r,Z}(\kappa^T_X)^{-1}.$$
Indeed take a pair $(b,a)$ of tuples of sections. On the left, its two coordinates are $(u_{r,n}b_n)_n$ and $(u_{r,n}a_n)_n$, interpreted as sections of the corresponding products. On the right, restriction on $Z^i=(\prod X_n^{i-1})\oplus(\prod X_n^i)$ is $(b,a)\mapsto((b_n|_{h^r})_n,(a_n|_{h^r})_n)$: restrictions in a sectionwise product are coordinatewise, and a finite direct sum is a finite product. The product comparison for $F_r$ and the finite-level identifications $j_r$ turn these coordinates into the same $u_{r,n}b_n,u_{r,n}a_n$ by [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent]. Equality holds in each degree of the full cone, not just after projection to individual derived evaluations.

proof.text:
Combine the chain-map equality in Step 7, the equation $\eta_YR\lim(I_{r,C})=H(u)\eta_X$ in Step 5, and the formulas of Step 4. Naturality of $\sigma$ for $\theta_X:\mathcal L_sC\to H(X)$ gives $\sigma_{r,H(X)}T(\theta_X)=T(F_r\theta_X)\sigma_{r,\mathcal L_sC}$. Substitution and cancellation of the consecutive inverse comparisons yield
$$\zeta_{G_rC}R\lim(I_{r,C})=T(a_{r,C})\sigma_{r,\mathcal L_sC}\zeta_C.$$
The normalized Roos comparisons descend by [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], and $u$ descends naturally by [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent]. Every construction used is natural for strict chain maps; it consequently commutes with inverted quasi-isomorphisms and with their composites, hence with all morphisms of $D(\mathscr S_s)$. This also proves independence of the representative $M$. No step used completeness, cartesianness, constructibility, boundedness or a Tor-amplitude bound on $C$ or $\mathcal L_sC$.
